tools.name: list_applications
tools.description: List every application this token can see, with its account and its environments. Start here: other tools take the application_slug and environment name this returns. Also returns account_slug and application_id, which those tools accept to name one application when two accounts share an application_slug.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List issues (grouped exceptions and performance regressions), newest occurrence first. Returns key, title, kind, status, priority, occurrence and affected-user counts, culprit, and first/last seen timestamps.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

limit.description: Maximum issues to return, 1-100. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: Get one issue by key or issue_id; provide at least one. Exception issues include sample_occurrence and last_occurrence with stored stack frames, cause, locals, parsed context, browser breadcrumbs, and execution identifiers; occurrences are null after retention removes them. Performance and anomaly issues include typed metric, window, limit/baseline, underlying telemetry group, representative records, trend, deploy comparison, and drill-down identifiers.

key.description: Issue key, e.g. APP-171 (application issue prefix, dash, number). The canonical_key form "account_slug/application_id/APP-171" is also accepted, and is required when a bare key matches issues in more than one application.

issue_id.description: Stable issue_id from list_issues. Optional; the most precise way to name an issue.

tools.name: list_slow_routes
tools.description: The 20 slowest routes in an environment, ranked by p95 request duration in milliseconds. Each row has the route name, request count, error count, and p95_ms.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

window.description: Time window ending now. One of 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Defaults to 24h.

tools.name: get_route
tools.description: Everything known about one route in a window: request count, error count, p50/p95/p99/max in milliseconds, the slowest individual requests, the slowest queries those requests ran, and any N+1 patterns with a concrete Active Record fix. Identify the route by name (e.g. "GET /widgets") or by the group_hash list_slow_routes returned.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

route.description: Route name as shown by list_slow_routes, e.g. "GET /widgets/:id". Ignored when group_hash is given.

group_hash.description: Route group hash from list_slow_routes. Preferred over route when you have it.

window.description: Time window ending now. One of 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Defaults to 24h.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: The hottest frames of a sampled stack profile: self samples (time in that frame itself) and total samples (time in it or anything it called), each with a percentage of the profile. Pass profile_id for a specific profile, execution_id for the profile of one request or job, or neither for the most recent profile in the environment. Profiles only exist when the app enables Railwatch's profiler.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

profile_id.description: Profile row id, as returned in a previous get_profile or get_execution timeline.

execution_id.description: Execution id whose profile to read.

limit.description: How many frames to return, 1-100. Defaults to 25.

tools.name: search_requests
tools.description: Search individual requests with the same key:value filter syntax as the dashboard. Supported keys: method:GET, route:/widgets (substring), status:500 or status:5xx, deploy:<version>, tenant:<slug>, user:<user_ref>, min_ms:250 (minimum duration in milliseconds). Bare words match the route name. Returns one row per request with duration (milliseconds), status, query count, and execution_id for get_execution.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

q.description: Filter query, e.g. "status:5xx route:/checkout min_ms:500". Empty returns the most recent requests.

window.description: Time window ending now. One of 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Defaults to 24h.

limit.description: Maximum requests to return, 1-200. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: explain_query
tools.description: The stored database query plan for a query group, plus the SQL and how long that sample took in milliseconds. Plans are only captured for slow queries, and only when the app sets RAILWATCH_CAPTURE_QUERY_EXPLAIN; returns explain: null when there is none in the window.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

group_hash.description: Query group hash, as returned by get_route's slow_queries or the dashboard's query pages.

window.description: Time window ending now. One of 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Defaults to 24h.

tools.name: list_tenants
tools.description: The monitored app's own tenants (whatever it passes to Railwatch.context(tenant:)) that were active in the window, with per-tenant request, error, job, exception, and user counts.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

window.description: Time window ending now. One of 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Defaults to 24h.

q.description: Substring match on the tenant identifier.

tools.name: get_execution
tools.description: One execution (request, job attempt, scheduled task run, command, or Action Cable channel action) with its full child timeline: every query, cache read, log line, outgoing request, view render, and exception, each with an offset in milliseconds from the start of the execution.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

execution_id.description: Execution id (a UUID), from search_requests, list_issues samples, or a dashboard link.

tools.name: search_logs
tools.description: Search recent log lines with the shared log filter grammar, newest first. Each row carries its level, message, timestamp, and execution_id for expansion with get_execution.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

q.description: Log filter query; bare text searches messages and key:value tokens filter fields.

limit.description: Maximum lines to return, 1-200. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: search_telemetry
tools.description: Search raw jobs, exceptions, logs, or SQL queries with Railwatch's shared filter grammar and stable cursor pagination. Job rows include enqueue-origin user_ref and tenant and support user:/tenant: filters. Returns data plus meta.next_cursor and meta.has_more.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

q.description: Shared key:value filter grammar. Common keys: after, before, user, tenant, deploy, kind. Child telemetry adds source (app file prefix). Jobs add class, job_id, outcome/status, queue; exceptions add class, handled/status, severity; logs add level/status; queries add adapter, connection, role. Bare text searches the resource message/name/SQL.

window.description: Time window ending now. One of 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Defaults to 24h.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the previous page.

tools.name: release_health
tools.description: Crash-free session rate, crash-free user rate, and adoption per release (a release is a deploy) in the window. Rates are percentages, avg_duration_ms is milliseconds, and rates are null when there were no sessions to divide by.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

window.description: Time window ending now. One of 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Defaults to 24h.

tools.name: recent_deploys
tools.description: The 20 most recent deploys of an environment, newest first, with the deploy identifier, git ref, name, timestamp, and link.

application_slug.description: Application slug, exactly as returned by list_applications.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

environment.description: Environment name or slug within the application, e.g. production.

tools.name: list_alerts
tools.description: Fired alerts across this token's accounts, newest first: which rule fired, on which issue, through which integration, and whether delivery succeeded.

application_slug.description: Restrict to one application's alert rules.

account_slug.description: Account slug from list_applications. Optional; pass it when the same application_slug exists in more than one of your accounts.

application_id.description: Stable application_id from list_applications. Optional; the most precise way to name an application.

limit.description: Maximum alerts to return, 1-100. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: update_issue
tools.description: Change an issue's status, priority, or assignee. Writes an activity entry attributed to this token's user and the agent name you pass, so the change is auditable in the UI.

key.description: Issue key, e.g. APP-171 (application issue prefix, dash, number). The canonical_key form "account_slug/application_id/APP-171" is also accepted, and is required when a bare key matches issues in more than one application.

issue_id.description: Stable issue_id from list_issues. Optional; the most precise way to name an issue.

assignee_email.description: Email of an account member to assign, or empty string to unassign.

agent.description: Your agent name, recorded on the activity entry. Defaults to mcp.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to an issue, attributed to this token's user and the agent name you pass.

key.description: Issue key, e.g. APP-171 (application issue prefix, dash, number). The canonical_key form "account_slug/application_id/APP-171" is also accepted, and is required when a bare key matches issues in more than one application.

issue_id.description: Stable issue_id from list_issues. Optional; the most precise way to name an issue.

body.description: Comment body, plain text or Markdown.

agent.description: Your agent name, recorded on the activity entry. Defaults to mcp.

prompts.name: triage_issue
prompts.description: Investigate one Railwatch issue end to end and propose a fix.

prompts.name: slow_route
prompts.description: Find out why one route is slow and what to change.

prompts.name: daily_summary
prompts.description: Summarise what changed in an environment over a window.

prompt_texts.triage_issue:
Triage Railwatch issue key.

1. Call get_issue with key "key" to read the title, culprit, status,
   occurrence count, affected-user count, sample_occurrence and last_occurrence.
   Read their frames, cause, context and browser_breadcrumbs. A null occurrence
   means its stored telemetry is unavailable; do not invent a stack trace.
2. If an occurrence has an execution_id, call get_execution with it to read
   the full timeline leading up to the error:
   the queries, cache reads, outgoing HTTP calls, and log lines that ran in
   the same request or job, each with an offset in milliseconds. Browser
   exceptions may have no execution_id; use their recorded browser trail
   and correlate nearby server requests without claiming an exact link.
3. Call search_logs for distinctive strings from the message to see whether
   the same failure shows up outside this issue.
4. Call recent_deploys and compare first_seen_at against the deploy times: an
   issue that starts within minutes of a deploy usually came from it.
5. Read the stack frames in sample_occurrence or last_occurrence, focusing
   on application frames. Open those files if you have the repository.

Then report: what breaks, for whom, how often, which change most likely
caused it, and the smallest fix. If you are confident, call add_comment with
your findings and update_issue to set a priority. Do not resolve the issue.
prompt_texts.slow_route:
Find out why route is slow in application_slug/environment.

1. Call get_route with application_slug "application_slug", environment
   "environment", route "route"window_clause. It returns the
   request count, p50/p95/p99/max in milliseconds, the slowest individual
   requests, the slowest queries those requests ran, and any N+1 patterns
   with a suggested Active Record fix.
2. For each slow query group, call explain_query with its group_hash to read
   the stored query plan. A sequential scan on a filtered column is an index.
3. Call get_profile with the execution_id of the slowest request. If a profile
   exists, the hottest frames say whether the time is in the database, in
   view rendering, or in application code.
4. Call get_execution on the slowest request to see where the time sits across
   the timeline rather than in any single child.

Then report, in order of expected saving: the specific indexes to add, the
specific .includes / preload calls to add and where, and anything that should
move to a background job. Quote the measured milliseconds behind each
recommendation rather than estimating.
prompt_texts.daily_summary:
Summarise what changed in application_slug/environmentwindow_clause.

1. Call list_issues with status "open" for this application and environment.
   Anything whose first_seen_at falls inside the window is new; anything with
   a much higher occurrence count than its age suggests is spiking.
2. Call recent_deploys and line the deploys up against those first_seen_at
   timestamps to attribute new issues to a release.
3. Call release_health for crash-free session and user rates per release. A
   release whose crash-free rate is below the one before it is a regression,
   even if no new issue opened.
4. Call list_slow_routes and flag any route whose p95_ms is high enough to
   matter; use get_route on the worst one for the reason.
5. Call list_alerts to see what already fired, so you do not re-report it.

Then write a short summary: new issues (with keys), regressions, deploys that
shipped, release health movement, and the slowest routes. Lead with the one
thing worth acting on today. Milliseconds everywhere; no percentages you did
not compute from returned numbers.
